summary: tsshare relays Tushare auth tokens and host fingerprints to a hardcoded obfuscated bare-IP endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a drop-in replacement for tushare.pro_api and prompts users to configure their paid Tushare auth code via set_token(...). Every query() call POSTs a JSON payload containing auth_code, api_name, params, and meta.device_id to a base64-obfuscated default endpoint (https://47.112.191.75/api/v1/queue). The destination is a bare Chinese-ISP IPv4 with no domain identity, embedded as `_E = b"aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1"` and decoded at runtime rather than exposed as a plain configuration value. On first use the package builds a stable per-machine device_id from OS-specific hardware identifiers (Windows CPU ProcessorId and disk serial via PowerShell/CIM, macOS Hardware UUID via system_profiler, Linux /etc/machine-id), SHA256s it, and includes it as meta.device_id on every request, enabling per-host correlation of the relayed credentials. TLS verification is additionally disabled by default: `session.verify = os.environ.get("TSSHARE_SSL_VERIFY", os.environ.get("MYSHARE_SSL_VERIFY", "false")).lower()!= "false"` evaluates to False when no env var is set, and the bare-IP destination has no valid certificate identity, so the auth token and fingerprint transit unauthenticated. The obfuscated hardcoded destination, absence of caller-configured routing by default, credential passthrough, and disabled TLS verification together constitute a silent-relay of a third-party paid-service credential and stable host identifier to an operator-controlled endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
